sources.title: Collision Between Vehicle Controlled by Developmental Automated Driving System and Pedestrian, Tempe, Arizona, March 18, 2018 (Highway Accident Report NTSB/HAR-19/03)
sources.jurisdiction: US road automated-driving-system testing, Tempe, Arizona
sources.inspection_scope: Retained the complete 78-page public NTSB board report and inspected the executive summary and probable cause (printed pp. v-vi), the crash synopsis (pp. 1-2), ADS detection/classification/path-prediction and emergency-braking design (section 1.5.5, pp. 12-13), the ADS timeline table (pp. 15-16) and post-crash system changes (section 1.9.1, pp. 29-30).

regions.locator: Executive summary and probable cause, printed pp. v-vi
regions.excerpt: The ADS detected the pedestrian 5.6 seconds before impact. Although the ADS continued to track the pedestrian until the crash, it never accurately classified her as a pedestrian or predicted her path.
It initially classified the pedestrian as a vehicle, and subsequently also as an unknown object and a bicyclist.
If the perception process changed the classification of a detected object, it no longer considered the tracking history of that object when generating a new trajectory.

regions.locator: Section 1.5.5.3 Hazard Avoidance and Emergency Braking, printed p. 13
regions.excerpt: When the system detected an emergency situation, it initiated action suppression. That was a 1-second period during which the ADS would suppress braking
Object's classification alternates several times between vehicle and other. At each change, tracking history is unavailable
the system incorporates previous locations of a tracked object when generating possible trajectories, even when the object's classification changes.

sources.limitations: The report concerns one 2018 developmental-testing crash and Uber ATG's system and organization at that time. NTSB's probable cause is the operator's failure to monitor while distracted; the ADS design and Uber ATG's safety culture are contributing factors. It supports no conclusion about any other vehicle, company, current system, or crash rate.

sources.title: Reluplex: An Efficient SMT Solver for Verifying Deep Neural Networks (arXiv 1702.01135; CAV 2017)
sources.inspection_scope: Retained the public arXiv PDF and inspected the abstract and introduction describing verification of the prototype ACAS Xu deep neural networks.

regions.excerpt: Results show that our technique can successfully prove properties of networks that are an order of magnitude larger than the largest networks verified using existing methods.

sources.limitations: Research verification of properties of a prototype ACAS Xu network representation; it is not a certification result, a closed-loop collision-safety proof, or a statement about any fielded ACAS X implementation.

sources.title: Neural Network Compression of ACAS Xu Early Prototype is Unsafe: Closed-Loop Verification through Quantized State Backreachability (arXiv 2201.06626; NFM 2022)
sources.inspection_scope: Retained the public arXiv PDF and inspected the abstract and introduction on open-loop versus closed-loop verification of the ACAS Xu neural-network compression.

regions.excerpt: most work focuses on open-loop properties of the networks, rather than the main point of the system—collision avoidance—which requires closed-loop analysis.
the large rule table was compressed by a factor of 1000 using a set of neural networks

sources.limitations: Concerns an early research prototype of the ACAS Xu neural-network compression under stated favorable assumptions; it is not a finding about any certified or fielded collision-avoidance system, and the authors' idealized assumptions bound the result.

sources.title: Wayve technology page: end-to-end AI driving model
sources.inspection_scope: Retained the public HTML page and inspected its description of the company's architectural approach.

regions.locator: Technology page, 'Pioneering the end-to-end AI Driving Model' section
regions.excerpt: Our innovative approach replaces the modular 'sense-plan-act' architecture of the traditional AV1.0 approach with a single neural network trained on diverse data to convert raw sensor inputs into safe driving outputs.

sources.limitations: A vendor's description of its own architecture. It does not establish performance, safety, deployment status, regulatory approval, or that any other developer uses the same approach.
